title: Insured Properties, Assisted Developers and Protected Landmarks

context_sources.name: Munich Re Natural Disaster Loss Record 2023
context_sources.role: Global losses of 250 billion dollars for 2023

context_sources.name: Zhang, Li and Zhang, information diffusion risk assessment
Shang Aiqun, valuation of Huizhou residences
context_sources.role: The economic value of the case buildings

limitations: A MATHmodels watermark of repeated glyphs runs through every page and through the equations.
Equations 1 to 41 print with sums and indices separated by placeholder blocks.
Figure 1 is the flowchart but the prose later points the grey-model test to Figure 2, whose caption reads Figure 4.
The letter quotes the maintenance cost as 27.0 million dollars and as 291,000 dollars against the model's 270,000.
The siting model gives neither weights nor a scored site.

tasks: Decide whether an insurer should underwrite each of two regions on different continents, and at what rate
Decide where a property developer should site buildings once resilience and sustainability costs count
Value a historic building that cannot get cover and choose the cheapest way to preserve it
Write the community a letter with the plan, the timeline, and the cost

section_map.summary: Three chained models, two regions underwritten, one building kept by maintenance.
Munich Re's 2023 record, then four named disasters.
Three tasks, the last one ending in a letter.
Profit maximization, a steady discount rate, one representative person.
A short table, the rest deferred to the point of use.
Information diffusion, a risk index, discounted profit, and a sign test.
A zero-profit curve, then Sichuan and Slovakia both underwritten.
Resilience and sustainability folded into four indicators, ranked by TOPSIS.
Fuzzy value and four costed options over ten years.
A value of 1.055 million dollars and maintenance as the cheapest option.
A ten-year plan with work in years three, four, seven, and eight.
Three parameters moved in six proportions, none said to matter much.

contributions.summary: The diffusion kernel widens automatically when the loss sample is small.
The underwriting decision is the sign of profit discounted over many years.
A resilience coefficient shrinks the insured loss to the share of the building that fails.
Five siting criteria are folded into four by argument rather than by dropping one.
Four conservation options are priced on one discounted basis and the cheapest is taken.

dependency_graph.handoff: The regional risk index and the discount rate enter the siting score and the adjusted profit.
The regional risk sets the building's loss rate and the discount rate prices the ten-year cost.

assumptions.summary: The discount rate will not fluctuate significantly.
Every policy is fair and full.
One rational individual represents the whole region.
Neighboring value grades differ by the same amount of money.
A relocated building faces essentially no further loss.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Munich Re's 2023 loss record: 250 billion dollars of losses, 95 billion insured, 74,000 deaths.
An insured amount of 2,000,000 thousands of dollars, losses of 750,000 thousands per event, discount rate 8 percent.
Sichuan for 1999 to 2020 and Slovakia for 2004 to 2020.
Huizhou climate: 16 degrees and 1,708 millimetres of rain, with more than 300 ancient buildings.
Construction costs taken from Chinese standards: 0.05 percent, 16.83 percent, and 300,000 dollars.

models.summary: Decides underwriting from the sign of discounted profit.
Ranks sites by TOPSIS after folding five criteria to four.
Values a building by fuzzy grades and picks the cheapest conservation option.

verification.summary: The grey forecast is tested by precision, variance ratio, and small-probability error.
Sichuan's variance ratios are 0.1624 and 0.1527; Slovakia's premium forecast reaches 0.7798.
Three parameters are each shifted in six proportions and the premium rate barely moves.

results_trace.summary: The insurer underwrites only when the premium rate lies above the zero-profit curve.
Discounted premiums exceed discounted claims in every month for both Sichuan and Slovakia.
The Huizhou residences are valued at 1.055 million dollars and graded very important.
The four option costs are about 270, 295, 300, and 390 thousand dollars, so maintenance wins.

writing_logic.summary: Put both parties in the same predicament before naming a model.
Chain the three models so each one is said to grow out of the last.
Open on a dated report and set one loss figure between two averages.
Rule out the obvious answer, the safest land, before building the model.
Fold a criterion into another instead of dropping it.
Price every option in the letter before recommending one.
Split one planning horizon into dated intervals, each with its own action.

language_observations.summary: The interaction is argued as on the one hand and on the other hand, so neither party is only a cause.
The turn to a fuzzy method is motivated by saying value lives in more than brick and tile.
The loss rates are ordered in a sentence before the formula uses them.
Each method is credited with repairing a stated fault of the other.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1 draws the whole argument as one flowchart.
Figure 2 maps global direct economic losses from extreme weather.
Figure 3 draws the zero-profit curve of disaster count against premium rate.
Figure 4 plots the grey forecast against the actual premiums and claims.
Figure 5 draws the roadmap between insurers and property developers.
Figure 6 shows the five indicators folding into four.
Figure 7 shows Huizhou ancient city and its buildings.
Figure 8 shows the sensitivity of the premium rate to three parameters.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A judge rewards an underwriting rule that reduces to the sign of one discounted sum.
A judge rewards criteria that are combined by argument instead of dropped.
A judge penalizes a letter whose costs contradict the model's own table.

weaknesses.summary: The grey-model test is said to appear in Figure 2, but that figure's caption reads Figure 4.
Regional property demand is abbreviated DPR once and RPD elsewhere.
The siting model never states its weights and never scores a site.
The letter prices maintenance at 27.0 million dollars and at 291,000 dollars against the model's 270,234.
The sensitivity test reports no numeric change for any of the six shifts.
Slovakia's premium forecast fails the variance test the paper itself applies, with a ratio of 0.7798.

independent_extensions.statement: Recompute the Huizhou option costs from the stated loss rates and replace the three conflicting figures in the letter with the one result.
independent_extensions.reason: The letter quotes 27.0 million, 291,000, and the model 270,234 dollars for the same option.

independent_extensions.statement: Estimate the TOPSIS weights from a stated comparison matrix and score at least two candidate sites.
independent_extensions.reason: The siting model is fully specified but never run, so it supports no decision.

candidate_rule_impacts.impact: Supports letting a diffusion kernel widen as the loss sample shrinks, and discounting the underwriting decision over many years.
Supports an underwriting rule defined as the sign of discounted profit, and a conservation choice defined as the minimum of four discounted costs.

unresolved_questions: Which maintenance cost, 270 thousand, 291 thousand, or 27 million dollars, the letter intends.
What weights the siting model would have used, since none are computed.
Whether Slovakia should be underwritten when its own forecast fails the variance test.
